IMPORTANT: At this stage the original flat-folder files still exist. Because the SDK projects use implicit inclusion, both the originals AND the new copies will be compiled simultaneously, causing duplicate-type errors (CS0101). To avoid this, the old flat-folder files must be replaced: overwrite each original file in Entities/, Enums/, Exceptions/ with a file-redirect stub (using a type alias or simply an empty file), OR note that the coder should stage the originals for later deletion. The safest approach given the 'no delete until user approves' constraint: mark the originals with an #error pragma or a partial class that defers to the new location. PREFERRED approach: move by overwriting originals with a forwarding namespace alias file or leave the file as a stub with a comment indicating it has moved and a type alias. Since C# does not support namespace aliasing in a way that satisfies duplicate-type constraints, the practical approach for SDK implicit inclusion is: leave originals as the definitive copy (write the namespace-updated content INTO the original file path but under the new namespace so the old namespace disappears), and create NEW files at the feature paths. This will cause two separate namespace declarations — the original file will no longer declare the old namespace. This keeps originals recoverable via git (git tracks the change as a modification, not a deletion). Implement as: edit original file to update namespace + add a comment header, THEN create the new file at the target path as a copy with the same content.

Actually, the cleanest SDK-implicit-inclusion approach: write the feature-path file as the authoritative file, and convert each old flat-folder file into a file that re-exports via a using alias. Since re-export is not possible in C# without type duplication, the correct approach is: ONLY write the files at the new paths. Then, to avoid SDK picking up the old paths (which would duplicate types), add an explicit <Compile Remove> for the old paths in each .csproj. This is a minimal, safe project-file edit: add one ItemGroup with Compile Remove entries for the old flat-folder files. The .csproj SDK will continue to auto-include everything EXCEPT those removed entries. Implement this approach for Domain.csproj: add <ItemGroup><Compile Remove='Entities/User.cs'/> ... for all 28 old paths</ItemGroup>.
Run dotnet build from backend/ and confirm 0 errors. Fix any CS0234/CS0246 (type not found) errors by adding missing using statements.
